text: On 20 May 2025, members of INC, led by the Pradesh Congress committee president and local MLAs, held a demonstration and clashed with police in Mandsaur town (Madhya Pradesh) against the unilateral action of local police against INC members after a clash with BJP members during the May 17 demonstration (coded separately).

On 3 August 2025, a group of Bhil leaders took out a demonstration rally in the Khandia area in Jhalawar city (Jhalawar, Rajasthan) during which some rioters clashed with the demonstrators demanding that the Banswara MP who was present stop promoting the Bharat Adivasi Party ideology at the community event. Police used lathicharge (baton charge) to disperse the two groups. The Banswara MP claimed that the disruptors were from the BJP and ABVP.

On 25 September 2025, villagers tried to vandalize a roadways bus, blocked the Alwar-Sikandra mega highway, and held a five-hour-long demonstration in the Baswa area (Dausa, Rajasthan), after the murder of a woman over a land dispute (coded separately). The agitation ended after authorities assured action against the accused, financial compensation, and a government job for the deceased's dependent son.

On 22 December 2024, students affiliated to the Osmania University Joint Action Committee staged a demonstration and vandalized an actor's residence in the Jubilee Hills locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana demanding justice for a victim of a stampede in movie theater where the actor made a special appearance. The demonstrators held placards, raised slogans climbed over the walls and pelted stones.

Around 28 April 2025 (as reported), members of the tribal organization burnt the effigy of the Chief Minister, clashed with the police, and held a demonstration in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) against the construction of a flyover ramp in Sirmatoli.

On 25 September 2025, villagers, after a fatal attack by a leopard, blocked the Keshori-Navegaon road, damaged government vehicles, and held a demonstration in Gothangaon village (Gondia, Maharashtra), demanding the immediate capture of the leopard and compensation for the deceased's family.

On 9 July 2025, members of RJD and CPI (Marxist), as part of Bihar Bandh (shutdown strike) called by Mahagathbandhan, raised slogans, held chakka jam (road blockades), burned tires, and staged demonstrations in Maner town (Patna, Bihar), against the Election Commission of India (ECI), which initiated special, intensive voter list revision in Bihar.

On 29 December 2024, Kuki-Zo womenfolk staged a demonstration and formed barricades along Thamnapokpi Uyokching and Yaingangpokpi Uyokching hill areas (coded to Thamnapokpi village, Imphal East, Manipur) to prevent Manipur police, Indian Army, BSF and CRPF personnel from entering their areas to conduct search operations, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Security forces broke through the barricades and occupied the bunkers.

On 18 December 2024, over 1000 INC members and supporters staged a demonstration rally towards the Raj Bhavan as a part of INC's nationwide 'Raj Bhavan Chalo' (Raj Bhavan march) in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) demanding the BJP-led Union government to address the Adani group's bribery accusations, the ongoing violence in Manipur and the installation of smart meters in Assam. Police personnel used tear gas shells at demonstrators after they attempted to break through police barricades and clashed with them, resulting in the injuries of many journalists who were covering the event including 3 who were severely injured while an INC State Congress Legal Cell member died from the side effects of the gas. Claims of the usage of expired tear gas canisters were made due to the symptoms faced by many present at the event while police refuted claims. Police also detained Assam INC's Chief and a former Rajya Sabha Member of Parliament (MP).

Around 20 March 2025 (as reported), tribal women organized a raid, seized illicit alcohol bottles from local vendors, raised slogans, marched through villages, threw the bottles into the river, and destroyed them in Katak village (Raisen, Madhya Pradesh) during a demonstration against the unchecked liquor trade.

On 5 April 2025, members of the political parties, including Lahuji Shakti Sena, Akhand Maratha Samaj, Nirbhay Maharashtra Party (Maratha group), Rugna Hakka Parishad (Patient Rights Council), and Satayshodhak Bahujan Aghadi (Dalit group), gathered removed shirts, raised slogans, threw stones at the Deenanath Mangeshkar Hospital building, and held a demonstration in Pune city (Maharashtra), after a pregnant woman died due to alleged denial of treatment for non-fulfillment of the expenses.

On 10 July 2025, hundreds of drivers, during an ongoing strike by the drivers' association, held a mass demonstration and detained fuel tankers at the Saintala locality near Titlagarh town (Balangir, Odisha), over unresolved grievances related to work conditions and transport issues.

On 26 January 2025, locals held police officials captive in Jogisarda village (Balangir district, Odisha) during a demonstration against the police's arrest of five locals in an arson incident in the village.
On 21 March 2025, women held a demonstration and hit the car of a BJP leader at Kharagpur town (Paschim Medinipur district, WB) over the lack of development in his constituency.

Around 20 March 2025 (as reported), tribal women organized a raid, seized illicit alcohol bottles from local vendors, raised slogans, marched through the village, threw the bottles into the river, and destroyed them in Jamanjhiri village (Raisen, Madhya Pradesh) during a demonstration against the unchecked liquor trade.

On 17 July 2025, Gulf migrant workers and members of INC staged a demonstration in Velpur village (Nizamabad, Telangana) against attacks on Gulf migrant workers. Members of BRS including an MLA attacked the migrant workers and INC members, and two INC members sustained injuries. The BRS members accused the migrant workers of attacking them.

On 5 December 2024, locals (likely Meitei based on demands) staged a road block demonstration by placing trees, bamboos and boulders on the road at Lamshang village (Imphal West, Manipur) attempting to block CRPF personnel from transferring arrested armed Meitei assailants to Imphal and demanded their release amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 5 December 2024, locals (likely Meitei based on demands) staged a road block demonstration by placing trees, bamboos and boulders on the road at Iroisemba on the outskirts of Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) attempting to block CRPF personnel from transferring arrested armed Meitei assailants to Imphal and demanded their release amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 5 December 2024, a large number of locals (likely Meitei based on demands) staged a road block demonstration by placing trees, bamboos and boulders on the road at Kangchup village (Imphal West, Manipur) attempting to block CRPF personnel from transferring arrested armed Meitei assailants to Imphal and demanded their release amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Security forces (likely police based on their presence in the region) fired tear gas shells and mock bombs to disperse the crowd.

On 19 November 2024, a local independent candidate, his father, and about 300 supporters entered and hackled the Bhartiya Janata Party national general secretary at a local hotel in Nala Sopara town (Palghar, Maharashtra) against his claimed involvement in 'cash-for-votes scandal'.

On 10 December 2024, farmers of Kumbhari village and members of the Samyukta Krushak Sangathan (United Farmers Organization) locked the chief civil supplies officer (CSO) inside his office for an hour in Bargarh town (Odisha) during a demonstration over a delay in paddy procurement.

On 14 September 2025, farmers staged a demonstration in Pragati Singaram village (Warangal Rural, Telangana) against the INC-led state government over non-availability of urea for fertilizers. The demonstrators set fire to urea bags to mark their demonstration.

On 19 July 2025, members of the Foothills Naga Coordination Committee (FNCC) started an indefinite strike, blocked roads with woods and stones and shouted slogans in the Naga-inhabited areas of Manipur (coded to Imphal city, Imphal West, Manipur) accusing Kuki militants of constructing unauthorized roads, camps for Kuki militants under Suspension of Operation (SoO) and against the poppy cultivation in the region, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. The Kuki-Zo Council (KZC) denied claims that the routes were used for drug trafficking, stating the route was an old inter-village track developed to aid Kuki-Zo civilians reach Kangpokpi, Chandel, and Tengnoupal districts from Churachandpur, avoiding Meitei-dominated areas. FNCC called off the blockade on 8 August following an agreement with Manipur government.

On 10 March 2025, dozens of Tibetan protesters clashed with the police outside the Chinese Embassy in Delhi - New Delhi city (New Delhi, Delhi), as Tibetans living in exile marked the 66th anniversary of their uprising against China that was crushed by Chinese forces.

On 26 July 2025, members of the Bajrang Dal forcefully entered the house of a Muslim family and raised slogans in Pune city (Maharashtra), demanding proof of their Indian citizenship and accusing them of being 'illegal immigrants'. The family members also claimed that the Bajrang Dal members were accompanied by police in plain clothes. Police refused the claim.

On 13 July 2025, Shivdharm Foundation (Hindu non-profit) supporters staged a demonstration, shoved, and threw ink at the Sambhaji Brigade leader in Akkalkot city (Solapur, Maharashtra), over his reported remarks on Swami Samarth.

Around 13 September 2025 (as reported), farmers staged a protest at local Agri center in Dornakal town (Mahabubabad, Telangana) against the INC-led state government over non-availability of urea for fertilizers. The protesters clashed with the police (likely non-violent based on lack of injuries).

On 27 January 2025, hundreds of SFI members held a demonstration and engaged in scuffle with the police at Salt Lake area in Bidhannagar town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) against TMC over claimed corruption and irregularities in the education system and teacher recruitment process in the state. Police detained 50 demonstrators. Many women members were beaten up by the police.

Around 3 November 2024 (as reported), people (likely Hindu based on the place of worship that was vandalized) held a road blockade and forced shops to close in Odisha (coded to Bhubaneswar city, Khordha) during a protest against the vandalism of 200-year-old place of worship in the state (coded separately).

On 3 January 2025, members of the CPI-ML, Congress, and the All India Students Union (AISU) along with an INC MP and a CPI(ML) MLA joined the students broke barricades at the JP roundabout in Gandhi Maidan, and marched towards Dak Bungalow Chowk in Patna city (Bihar), demanding the re-conduct of the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) 70th Preliminary Test (PT) over claimed irregularities. Supporters of an INC MP also staged a separate protest at the railway tracks near Sachiwalay halt in Patna city.

On 24 June 2025, hundreds of farmers, under the banner of BKU, staged a protest march, raising slogans, from Parivartan Chowk (intersection) to the Gandhi statue in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) over various issues including failed cow shelters, corruption, and fake fertilizers. The protesters clashed with the police (likely non-violent due to lack of injuries).

On 10 May 2025, a group of youngsters, including some students, under the aegis of Indian People in Solidarity with Palestine (IPSP)'s Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) campaign held placards and staged a demonstration in front of a pizza joint in Karvenagar in Pune city (Maharashtra), over the pizza joint's 'support' of the 'genocide' in Gaza. Later, a group of right-wing activists (likely Hindu based on motive) and supporters of a local Bharatiya Janata Party leader questioned them and then assaulted them after reading their placards.

On 29 December 2024, the chairman of the Jan Suraaj party joined large numbers of aspirants in their demonstration march towards the chief minister's residence in Patna city (Bihar), demanding the cancellation of the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) 70th CCE-pre exam over claimed irregularities. The aspirants scuffled with police during the march, and police used baton charges and water cannons to stop it.

On 15 September 2025, hundreds of members of BJD tried to gherao (surround) the Raj Bhavan (governor's house), scuffled (likely non-violent due to lack of injuries) with police, and held a massive demonstration in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) over 'fertilizer shortage' faced by the farmers of the state. They later submitted a memorandum to the governor.

On 5 February 2025, BJP members staged a protest near the polling station at the Maujpur locality in the Delhi - Shahdara area (Shahdara, Delhi) over suspicions of fake voting at the polling station - for the assembly elections. The protesters clashed (likely non-violent due to lack of injuries and since the report does not describe any physical violence) with the police.

On 14 August 2025, local people, BJP members, and family members of the deceased staged a protest along the road and burned tires in Singur town (West Bengal) against the death of a woman (nurse), under suspicious circumstances, whom the protesters claimed was murdered. The woman's boyfriend was detained for questioning. The protesters also clashed (likely non-violent due to lack of injuries) with the police.

On 14 February 2025, members of ABVP and CPI(M) staged a protest in Kottayam city (Kerala) against the bullying and attack (coded separately) of a Scheduled Caste student. The protesters broke through police barricades and clashed with the police.

On 23 September 2025, BJD members and legislators broke two barricades along Gandhi Marg, scuffled with police, and held a protest outside the Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) over the claimed curtailment of powers of elected representatives under the three-tier Panchayati Raj system. Police used water cannons to disperse them when they tried to enter the Assembly. Several BJD workers were also detained.

On 25 March 2025, INC leaders, including former members of Parliament, held a demonstration and scuffled with police at the Assembly gate in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) against the suspension of 12 members of the legislative assembly from the Odisha Assembly over claimed disorderly conduct. IYC members burned effigies. Police detained the leaders.

On 12 September 2025, INC members staged the Kisan Annadata Samman Andolan (farmers forum) programme and burned the CM's photograph on the funeral bier outside Sondwa Police Station in Sondwa village (Alirajpur, Madhya Pradesh), demanding compensation for the farmers' damaged crops.
